title: Blindboard v1: environment, harness, and evidence
description:
Code and data release for Blindboard: Measuring State Tracking Under Interference with a Hidden, Shifting Keyboard (Allcock, 2026). Blindboard tests whether a language model can keep track of facts that keep changing: a model presses keys on a keyboard whose layout is hidden, is told which symbols came back but not from which key, and keeps the layout current while the board reshuffles itself between turns.

The release contains the environment and its scripted reference solver, the harness that carries each model's own reasoning between turns, every scored episode of the retained-reasoning and visible-transcript campaigns with full transcripts, the diagnostics behind every published number, and rebuild.py, which regenerates every table and number in the paper from the stored episodes and checks them byte for byte (Python standard library only, no network).
